reason: The text describes primordial humanity (Adam and Eve) in Genesis 2-3, predating the existence of the Hebrew people as a nation. While the narrative does show Yahweh providing for humanity's immediate needs (food, shelter, companionship), the passage is fundamentally concerned with establishing divine authority and demonstrating the consequences of disobedience rather than expressing a goal to help the Hebrew people specifically. The narrative centers on transgression and punishment (expulsion from Eden, toil, suffering), not on a stated aim to assist the Hebrew people, who would not emerge as a distinct people until many generations later.
